# Fonju Law Firm

> Fonju Law Firm is a Douala-based international legal consultancy advising businesses across Cameroon and the CEMAC/OHADA zone on corporate law, investment, maritime, mining, IP, employment and litigation.

Fonju Law Firm is a law firm and legal consultancy in Douala, Cameroon. It advises companies, investors and individuals, in English and French, on Cameroonian law and on the OHADA and CEMAC regional frameworks. It acts as local counsel for foreign clients entering Cameroon and Central Africa.

## Key facts

- Name: Fonju Law Firm (Fonju Law Firm — International Legal Consultancy)
- Founded: 2014
- Founder and managing partner: Bar. Fonju Bernard
- Office: Rue Ernest Betote, Akwa, P.O. Box 15354, Douala, Cameroon
- Telephone: +237 699 96 41 77, +237 676 37 11 80 (WhatsApp on the first number)
- E-mail: info@fonjulawfirm.com
- Opening hours: Monday – Friday 8:00 AM – 7:30 PM; Saturday 8:00 AM – 12:00 PM; Sunday Closed
- Languages: English and French
- Jurisdictions: Cameroon (common law in the North West and South West regions, civil law elsewhere), the 17 OHADA member states, the CEMAC zone
- Website: https://fonjulawfirm.com/ (English) and https://fonjulawfirm.com/fr (French)
- Enquiries: answered within one business day; urgent matters the same day

## Practice areas

- [Corporate & Commercial Law](https://fonjulawfirm.com/practice/corporate-law): Company formation, governance, restructuring and day-to-day commercial counsel under the OHADA Uniform Acts.
- [Arbitration & Alternative Dispute Resolution](https://fonjulawfirm.com/practice/arbitration-and-adr): CCJA and ad hoc arbitration, mediation and negotiated settlements that resolve disputes without years in court.
- [Litigation & Settlements](https://fonjulawfirm.com/practice/litigation-and-settlements): Advocacy before Cameroonian courts at every level, from Courts of First Instance to the Supreme Court.
- [Investments & Securities](https://fonjulawfirm.com/practice/investments-and-securities): Fund formation, capital raising, securities regulation and investor protection in the CEMAC market.
- [Banking & Finance](https://fonjulawfirm.com/practice/banking): Lending, security, banking regulation and COBAC compliance for lenders and borrowers alike.
- [Financial Services & Fintech](https://fonjulawfirm.com/practice/financial-services): Payment services, mobile money, digital lending and the licensing pathways that make them lawful.
- [Insurance Law](https://fonjulawfirm.com/practice/insurance): CIMA Code compliance, policy drafting, broking regulation and contested claims.
- [Tax & Customs](https://fonjulawfirm.com/practice/tax-and-customs): Corporate tax structuring, VAT, transfer pricing, customs classification and tax dispute defence.
- [Bankruptcy & Insolvency](https://fonjulawfirm.com/practice/bankruptcy-and-insolvency): Preventive settlement, judicial reorganisation, liquidation and creditor recovery under OHADA.
- [Labour & Employment](https://fonjulawfirm.com/practice/labour-and-employment): Contracts, collective agreements, dismissals, expatriate staffing and labour inspectorate disputes.
- [Intellectual Property](https://fonjulawfirm.com/practice/intellectual-property): OAPI trade marks, patents and designs, copyright, trade secrets and enforcement against counterfeits.
- [Immigration & Naturalisation](https://fonjulawfirm.com/practice/immigration-and-naturalisation): Visas, residence permits, work authorisation, naturalisation and corporate mobility programmes.
- [Technology, Data & Telecoms](https://fonjulawfirm.com/practice/information-technology-and-telecommunications): Software and SaaS contracts, personal data protection, cybersecurity, licensing and telecoms regulation.
- [iGaming & Betting Regulation](https://fonjulawfirm.com/practice/igaming-and-betting): Licensing, compliance and structuring for online gaming, sports betting and lottery operators in Central Africa.
- [Real Estate & Property](https://fonjulawfirm.com/practice/real-estate-and-property): Land title verification, acquisitions, leases, construction contracts and property disputes.
- [Maritime & Shipping](https://fonjulawfirm.com/practice/maritime-and-shipping): Charterparties, cargo claims, vessel arrest, port operations and marine casualty response in the Gulf of Guinea.
- [Aviation](https://fonjulawfirm.com/practice/aviation): Aircraft leasing and finance, operator licensing, regulatory compliance and passenger claims.
- [Transport & Logistics](https://fonjulawfirm.com/practice/transport-and-logistics): Road and rail carriage, corridor transit, warehousing, customs clearance and freight liability.
- [Mining & Energy](https://fonjulawfirm.com/practice/mining-and-energy): Exploration and mining titles, petroleum contracts, power projects, renewables and environmental compliance.
- [Health Care & Life Sciences](https://fonjulawfirm.com/practice/health-care): Clinic and pharmaceutical regulation, medical liability, product approval and health data protection.
- [Media, Sports & Creative Industry](https://fonjulawfirm.com/practice/media-sports-and-creative-industry): Artist and athlete representation, image rights, broadcasting, sponsorship and content licensing.

## Articles

- [Registering a Company in Cameroon: What the Process Actually Looks Like](https://fonjulawfirm.com/insights/registering-a-company-in-cameroon): The official timeline says a few days. The realistic timeline depends on decisions you make before you ever reach the registry. Here is the sequence that works.
- [OHADA Explained: The Legal Framework Behind Every Cameroonian Business Deal](https://fonjulawfirm.com/insights/ohada-explained-for-business): Seventeen countries, one commercial code and a supranational court that can overturn your national judgment. A practical orientation for foreign and local businesses.
- [Buying Land in Cameroon: Seven Checks Before You Pay a Deposit](https://fonjulawfirm.com/insights/buying-land-in-cameroon-checklist): Land is the most disputed asset in Cameroon and the most frequently mis-sold. Almost every failure traces back to a check that was skipped before the deposit.
- [Dismissing an Employee in Cameroon: The Procedure That Protects the Employer](https://fonjulawfirm.com/insights/dismissing-an-employee-in-cameroon): Employers rarely lose dismissal cases because the reason was bad. They lose because the procedure was incomplete. The file has to be finished before anyone is told anything.
- [One Filing, Seventeen Countries: A Practical Guide to OAPI Trade Marks](https://fonjulawfirm.com/insights/oapi-trade-mark-guide): Cameroonian businesses have access to a regional registration system that is genuinely powerful and consistently underused. Here is how to use it well.
- [Arbitration or Court? Choosing a Dispute Resolution Clause That Works](https://fonjulawfirm.com/insights/arbitration-or-court-cameroon): The dispute resolution clause is negotiated last, in five minutes, by tired people. It then determines the entire economics of any dispute that follows.
- [Foreign Investment in Cameroon: Structures, Incentives and Getting Profits Out](https://fonjulawfirm.com/insights/foreign-investment-in-cameroon): Investors ask about incentives first. They should ask about repatriation first, because that is the constraint that shapes the whole structure.
- [Data Protection for Cameroonian Businesses: Where to Start](https://fonjulawfirm.com/insights/data-protection-cameroon-business): Enterprise customers and foreign partners now refuse to contract without adequate data terms. Compliance has quietly become a sales requirement.
- [iGaming in Central Africa: What Operators Should Expect from the Regulator](https://fonjulawfirm.com/insights/igaming-regulation-central-africa): Online gaming is growing faster than the legislation written to govern it. Operators who engage early consistently secure better terms than those who regularise later.

## Optional

- Q: How do I book a consultation with Fonju Law Firm? A: Call +237 699 96 41 77 or +237 676 37 11 80, send a message on WhatsApp, e-mail info@fonjulawfirm.com, or complete the enquiry form on our contact page. We aim to respond to every enquiry within one business day, and urgent matters — a vessel arrest, an arrest of a person, an imminent deadline — are handled the same day.
- Q: What happens during the first consultation? A: We listen first. You describe the situation, we ask questions, and by the end of the meeting you receive three things: our view of your legal position, the realistic options with their likely cost and timeline, and a clear recommendation. If we believe you do not need a lawyer, we will say so.
- Q: How are your fees calculated? A: We use hourly rates, fixed fees and retainers depending on the work. Transactional and advisory matters — incorporations, contracts, filings, due diligence — are usually quoted as a fixed fee so you know the cost before you commit. Litigation is normally billed on an agreed structure with defined stages. Whatever the model, you receive a written engagement letter setting out the fee, what it covers and what it excludes before work begins. We do not send surprise invoices.
- Q: Do you work in English and French? A: Yes. Cameroon operates a bijural system, with common law procedure in the North West and South West regions and civil law procedure elsewhere. Our team works in both English and French and is comfortable in both traditions, which matters when a matter crosses regions or involves foreign counterparties.
- Q: Is my information kept confidential? A: Yes. Communications with your lawyer are protected by professional secrecy under the rules governing advocates in Cameroon, and confidentiality is one of the obligations we take most seriously. Information you share with us in the course of seeking advice is not disclosed to any third party without your instruction, and that duty continues after the matter ends.
- Q: Can you act for clients outside Douala? A: Yes. Our office is in Douala, but we act for clients throughout Cameroon and appear before courts across the country. A great deal of advisory work is handled remotely by video call, e-mail and secure document exchange, and we travel for hearings and completions.
- Q: How long does it take to register a company in Cameroon? A: Registration at the RCCM through a Centre de Formalités de Création d'Entreprises can be completed quickly once the file is complete. The realistic timeline is driven by the preparatory work — deciding the corporate form, drafting the articles and shareholder arrangements, gathering and legalising identity documents, and depositing capital — and by any sector licence you need. For a straightforward SARL with documents in order, plan on a few weeks from first meeting to fully operational, including tax and CNPS registration.
- Q: Which company form should I choose: SARL, SA or SAS? A: The SARL suits most small and medium businesses: simple management, flexible capital, and it can be formed by a single member. The SA is required for certain regulated activities and expected by institutional investors, but carries higher capital and a formal board. The SAS offers the most contractual flexibility and is usually the best fit where outside investors are coming in. Choose with your two-year plan in mind — converting later costs time and can trigger tax consequences.

Note: the content of this website is general information about Cameroonian and OHADA law, not legal advice for a particular situation.
